scenario.title: Alstom Transport UK Ltd v London Underground Ltd
scenario.description: London Underground awarded contract to Bombardier for £112.1 million worth of AC traction motors and control equipment. Alstom challenged the award alleging a manifest error in applying a mandatory technical threshold requirement, which should have excluded Bombardier's bid. The challenge was brought during the standstill period, triggering an automatic suspension. London Underground applied to lift the suspension under the American Cyanamid framework, arguing that damages would be adequate remedy for Alstom if it succeeded at trial and that the balance of convenience favoured proceeding with the contract.

interests: Protection of Public Funds: £112.1 million contract value at stake
Continuity of Service / Delivery: Critical rail infrastructure delivery delayed by automatic suspension and potential re-run
Reputation & Public Accountability: Maintain public confidence in procurement process amidst high-profile challenge
ca_pre_negotiation.batna: Defend the decision in the TCC — costly (£50k+) and slow (6-12 months), with a real risk of automatic suspension.
ca_pre_negotiation.opening_position: We stand by our evaluation process and scoring, which was carried out fairly and in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023

interests: Commercial Loss & Recovery: £112.1 million contract value at stake
Fairness & Transparency: perceived manifest error in technical threshold requirement application
Protection of Reputation: bid team's performance and credibility are on the line
goals: Force a re-evaluation of submitted bids
bidder_pre_negotiation.batna: Pursue a damages claim in the TCC — costly (£50k-£100k in legal fees) for a business our size, slow, and the outcome is uncertain.
bidder_pre_negotiation.opening_position: Request an immediate re-evaluation of Bombardier's bid to address the alleged manifest error

messages.message: Alstom Transport UK Ltd has alleged a manifest error in applying a mandatory technical threshold requirement, which should have excluded Bombardier's bid. I would like to clarify whether Alstom is challenging the evaluation team's interpretation of this specific requirement or if there are any concerns regarding the transparency and consistency of its application throughout the procurement process.

I'd like to clarify whether London Underground applied the mandatory technical threshold requirement consistently throughout the procurement process. Can you provide an explanation for how this requirement was evaluated in each bid, specifically Bombardier's and Alstom's?

I acknowledge Alstom's concerns regarding the application of the mandatory technical threshold requirement and assure you that we will provide a detailed explanation on how this requirement was evaluated in each bid, specifically Bombardier's and Alstom's. Our evaluation team followed the published criteria strictly, and we are confident that our process was transparent and consistent throughout the procurement. We will share the specific scores and breakdowns for both bids, as well as the evaluation panel's deliberations, to address your concerns.

I appreciate London Underground's assurance that they followed the published criteria strictly and are confident in their process. However, I would like to request a more detailed explanation on how this requirement was evaluated in each bid, specifically Bombardier's and Alstom's. Can you provide a breakdown of the scores for each criterion under the mandatory technical threshold requirement? This will help me understand whether there were any inconsistencies in the application of this requirement across bids.

We will provide a detailed breakdown of the scores for each criterion under the mandatory technical threshold requirement for both Bombardier's and Alstom's bids, as well as the evaluation panel's deliberations. This will include specific scores and explanations for each criterion, including the Technical Capability, Design and Innovation, and Quality Assurance categories. We are confident that our process was transparent and consistent throughout the procurement, and we believe this information will address your concerns regarding the application of the mandatory technical threshold requirement.

I appreciate London Underground's willingness to provide a detailed breakdown of the scores for each criterion under the mandatory technical threshold requirement. However, I would like to request that this information be provided in a format that allows us to easily compare the evaluation of both bids. Specifically, can you provide a side-by-side comparison of the scores and explanations for each criterion, including Technical Capability, Design and Innovation, and Quality Assurance categories? This will help me understand whether there were any inconsistencies in the application of this requirement across bids.

We are pleased to provide a side-by-side comparison of the scores and explanations for each criterion under the mandatory technical threshold requirement, as requested. This comparison will include specific scores and explanations for each criterion, including Technical Capability, Design and Innovation, and Quality Assurance categories, for both Bombardier's and Alstom's bids. We believe this information will address your concerns regarding the application of the mandatory technical threshold requirement.

I appreciate London Underground's willingness to provide a detailed breakdown of the scores for each criterion under the mandatory technical threshold requirement. However, upon reviewing the side-by-side comparison provided, I notice that Bombardier's bid received a higher score in the Technical Capability category despite Alstom's bid meeting all the mandatory requirements. This discrepancy raises concerns about the consistency of the evaluation process. I would like to request clarification on how this difference in scoring was justified and whether it had any impact on the overall evaluation outcome.

We acknowledge that the discrepancy in scoring between Bombardier's and Alstom's bids in the Technical Capability category raises concerns about consistency in the evaluation process. We are willing to re-evaluate the scores for this criterion, taking into account the mandatory technical threshold requirement. If our re-evaluation confirms that Alstom's bid meets all the mandatory requirements, we will reconsider the overall evaluation outcome and take appropriate action.
messages.proposal: A revised evaluation of the Technical Capability category, with a focus on ensuring consistency in the application of the mandatory technical threshold requirement

messages.message: I appreciate London Underground's willingness to re-evaluate the scores for the Technical Capability category and reconsider the overall evaluation outcome if Alstom's bid meets all the mandatory requirements. Given this development, I propose a partial award that covers 50% of the contract value, with the remaining 50% being reserved pending further review and potential re-award. This proposal aims to balance the need for fairness and consistency in the evaluation process with the desire to move forward with the procurement.
messages.proposal: A partial award covering 50% of the contract value

ca_win_statement.outcome_relative_to_batna: The negotiation outcome is a draw, neither party achieving their desired outcome. However, it avoided the costs and risks associated with proceeding to formal proceedings, which could have taken 6-12 months and cost £50k+.
ca_win_statement.win_statement: We successfully maintained our position on the evaluation process and demonstrated transparency in providing detailed explanations and score breakdowns. Although we did not achieve a full win, we avoided potential costs and risks associated with further litigation.

summary.concessions_summary: Both parties made concessions throughout the negotiation, but neither side was willing to compromise on their core positions. Alstom Transport UK Ltd requested a detailed breakdown of scores and explanations for each criterion under the mandatory technical threshold requirement, while London Underground Ltd provided this information in subsequent rounds. However, the Aggrieved Bidder continued to press for clarification on the scoring discrepancy in the Technical Capability category.
summary.court_reasoning_summary: The Court assessed each round qualitatively due to the lack of explicit formulas or sub-scores mentioned in the scenario. The Court found that London Underground's process followed the published criteria, but noted concerns about consistency and transparency in the evaluation process. However, without explicit scores or explanations for each criterion, it was difficult to determine whether these discrepancies raised concerns about the consistency of the evaluation process.
summary.likely_next_steps: Given the deadlock reached after Round 5, the dispute will likely escalate to formal proceedings. The Court's assessments suggest that both parties have made concessions and efforts to address the Aggrieved Bidder's concerns, but neither side has been willing to compromise on their core positions. Formal proceedings may provide a more detailed examination of the evaluation process and scoring discrepancies.
summary.plain_english_summary: The negotiation between Alstom Transport UK Ltd and London Underground Ltd centered around the application of a mandatory technical threshold requirement in the procurement process. Despite concessions made by both parties, the dispute reached a deadlock due to disagreements over the consistency of the evaluation process and scoring discrepancies. The Court's assessments suggest that formal proceedings may be necessary to resolve the dispute.
